forms: name the element from its job
say what a described element tells the reader
pick the element that answers a map question
find the wrong statement about a map element
SOCI.G5.NATURA.ELEMENTS_OF_A_MAP.MAP_ELE.mastery: Given a short description, the child names the title (what the map is about), the frame (the border), the scale (how far a distance on the map is on the ground), the compass (direction) and the key (what each symbol means), and does not swap scale and key or title and frame. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: read what a symbol means from a described key
use a scale to find a ground distance
give a direction from a described map
read a small table of map facts
SOCI.G5.NATURA.ELEMENTS_OF_A_MAP.MAP_REA.mastery: Given a map described in words or a small table, the child reads a symbol from the key, turns a map distance into a ground distance with the scale, and gives a direction. Map questions are in words or a small described table. The child does not guess a symbol from how it looks and does not read 1 cm as 1 km without the scale. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the country that borders Kenya
pick the list of all five neighbours
say which country does not border Kenya
spot the false step in a learner's list
SOCI.G5.NATURA.LOCATION_POSITION_AND_SI..mastery: The child names Ethiopia, South Sudan, Uganda, Tanzania and Somalia as the five countries that share a land border with Kenya, knows the Indian Ocean is water and not a neighbouring country, and does not add countries that are only near, such as Rwanda, Burundi, Zambia or the DR Congo. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say which direction a neighbour lies from Kenya
name the neighbour in a given direction
give the direction from a neighbour back to Kenya
read a small table of directions
SOCI.G5.NATURA.LOCATION_POSITION_AND_SI..mastery: The child places Ethiopia to the north, South Sudan to the north-west, Somalia to the east and north-east, Uganda to the west, Tanzania to the south and south-west, and the Indian Ocean to the south-east, and can turn the direction round (Kenya is east of Uganda). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say what kind of feature it is (mountain, lake, river, valley, ocean)
name the feature from a short description
pick the odd one out
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G5.NATURA.MAIN_PHYSICAL_FEATURES_I..mastery: The child names and classifies Mount Kenya (highest mountain in Kenya), Mount Elgon, the Aberdare Range, the Great Rift Valley, Lake Victoria, Lake Turkana, Lake Naivasha, the Tana and Athi rivers and the Indian Ocean coast, and knows Mount Kilimanjaro is in Tanzania. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the part of Kenya where a feature lies
name the feature at a described place
use a neighbour or the equator to place a feature
read a small table of places
SOCI.G5.NATURA.MAIN_PHYSICAL_FEATURES_I..mastery: Given a described map or table, the child places Lake Victoria in the west, Lake Turkana in the north-west, Mount Kenya in the central highlands on the equator, the Indian Ocean on the south-east coast, Mount Elgon on the Uganda border and the Rift Valley running north to south through the country. Map questions are in words or a small described table. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the instrument for an element
say whether a statement is about weather or climate
choose the element a reading describes
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G5.NATURA.WEATHER_AND_CLIMATE.WEATH.mastery: The child names temperature, rainfall, wind, humidity, cloud cover and sunshine as elements of weather, matches the thermometer, rain gauge, wind vane and sunshine recorder to what each measures, and knows weather is the condition of one day or place while climate is the usual pattern over many years. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: name the region of a described place
pick the place with a given climate
read a small table of towns and climates
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G5.NATURA.WEATHER_AND_CLIMATE.CLIMA.mastery: The child places the hot, dry arid and semi-arid regions in the north and east (Turkana, Marsabit, Wajir, Mandera), the hot humid region along the coast (Mombasa, Kilifi), the cool highland region around Mount Kenya and the Rift highlands (Nyeri, Kericho), and the warm, wet region around Lake Victoria and Kakamega. Map questions are in words or a small described table. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say which description fits a region
say which crop or activity fits a region
explain why a highland town is cool
read a small table of temperature and rainfall
SOCI.G5.NATURA.WEATHER_AND_CLIMATE.CLIMA.mastery: The child describes the arid north as hot with very little rain, the coast as hot and humid with plenty of rain, the highlands as cool with reliable rain, and Lake Victoria as warm with rain through most of the year, and explains that high places are cooler even near the equator. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: name the site from a description
say where a site is
say whether a place is built or natural
read a small table of sites
SOCI.G5.NATURA.THE_BUILT_ENVIRONMENTS.HI.mastery: The child names Fort Jesus (Mombasa, built by the Portuguese), Lamu Old Town, the Gedi Ruins (near Malindi), Thimlich Ohinga (stone enclosure in Migori) and the Nairobi National Museum, says where each is, and knows a mountain or lake is natural, not built. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the action that conserves a site
say why a visitor action harms a site
say who should look after a site
find the false step in a learner's plan
SOCI.G5.NATURA.THE_BUILT_ENVIRONMENTS.CO.mastery: The child picks actions that keep a site for later generations (repair with care, no writing or climbing on old walls, guides and visitor rules, teaching others, reporting damage) and rejects harming actions (taking stones, pulling down for new building, writing names). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the group a community belongs to
pick the list that belongs to one group
read a small table and sort a community
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G5.PEOPLE.LANGUAGE_GROUPS_IN_KENYA..mastery: The child puts the Kikuyu, Luhya, Kamba, Meru, Kisii and Mijikenda in the Bantu group; the Luo, Kalenjin, Maasai, Samburu and Turkana in the Nilotic group; and the Somali, Borana, Rendille and Gabra in the Cushitic group. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say what two communities exchange
say a benefit of depending on each other
say why no community can live alone
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G5.PEOPLE.LANGUAGE_GROUPS_IN_KENYA..mastery: The child gives true examples of exchange (herders trade milk, meat and hides for grain and vegetables; fishing communities trade fish for farm produce; Kiswahili and markets link communities) and explains that people share skills, goods and ideas, so no group lives alone. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say which area is crowded and which is thinly settled
pick the reason for high or low density
work out which area is denser from people and area
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G5.PEOPLE.POPULATION_DISTRIBUTION_..mastery: The child says density means people per square kilometre, that it is high in the central highlands, around Lake Victoria, the coast and Nairobi (good rain, fertile soil, jobs) and low in the dry north and east (little rain, poor soil), and does not mistake a big area for a high density. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick an effect of crowding
pick an effect of thin settlement
say which area an effect belongs to
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G5.PEOPLE.POPULATION_DISTRIBUTION_..mastery: The child gives effects of high density (small farms, pressure on land, water and housing, crowded schools and roads, easy markets and services) and of low density (few schools, clinics and roads, long distances, plenty of land for herding), and does not say one is all good or all bad. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: name the method from a story of a child learning
say what a method teaches
pick the method used in a described scene
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G5.PEOPLE.AFRICAN_TRADITIONAL_EDUC..mastery: The child names the methods: storytelling, proverbs, riddles, songs and dances, observation and imitation, learning by doing (apprenticeship), initiation and role play, and knows the elders, parents and community were the teachers. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say which value a practice teaches
say why traditional education still matters
pick a way to practise a value today
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G5.PEOPLE.AFRICAN_TRADITIONAL_EDUC..mastery: The child links practices to values (respect for elders, honesty, hard work, sharing, courage, responsibility), explains that traditional education prepared children for adult life in the community, and applies a value in school or at home. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say who does a duty
say what a leader does
pick the leader to see for a problem
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G5.PEOPLE.SCHOOL_ADMINISTRATION.ADM.mastery: The child names the headteacher (runs the whole school), the deputy headteacher (helps the head and acts when the head is away), senior teachers and heads of department (guide a subject or section), class teachers (look after a class and the register), the Board of Management (oversees development and discipline in a public school) and prefects (help keep order), and states a duty for each. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say who is above whom
say who reports to whom
finish a described chart
read a small table of ranks
SOCI.G5.PEOPLE.SCHOOL_ADMINISTRATION.ADM.mastery: The child puts the headteacher at the top of the school staff, then the deputy headteacher, senior teachers or heads of department, class and subject teachers, and learners with their prefects, and says who reports to whom. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say whether something is a natural resource
pick the resources a place has
sort resources into natural and made by people
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G5.RESOUR.RESOURCES_IN_KENYA.RESOUR.mastery: The child names land, soil, water, minerals, forests, wildlife, fish, sunshine and wind as natural resources of Kenya, and does not count money or buildings as natural resources. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the prudent action
say what sustainable means with an example
say what happens if a resource is used up
find the false step in a learner's plan
SOCI.G5.RESOUR.RESOURCES_IN_KENYA.PRUDEN.mastery: The child says using resources prudently means using them carefully so they last, and gives sustainable actions (plant trees to replace those cut, mend leaking taps, fish with proper nets, reuse and recycle, rotate crops), and knows that even forests and fish can finish if over-used. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: name the mineral mined at a place
name the place where a mineral is mined
say whether something is a mineral
read a small table of minerals
SOCI.G5.RESOUR.MINING_IN_KENYA.MINERAL_P.mastery: The child links soda ash to Lake Magadi, fluorspar to the Kerio Valley, titanium to Kwale, gemstones to Taita Taveta, limestone (for cement) to the coast and Athi River, gold to Kakamega and Migori, and says the oil found in Turkana is a mineral resource too. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say what a mineral is used for
say how mining helps the country
say a problem mining can cause
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G5.RESOUR.MINING_IN_KENYA.MINERAL_I.mastery: The child gives the uses of minerals (limestone for cement, soda ash for glass and soap, fluorspar for steel and chemicals, gemstones for jewellery), the gains from mining (jobs, money from sales, raw materials for industries, government income) and the harm mining can do if not controlled (damaged land, dust, unsafe pits). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the inland fishing ground
say where a lake lies
say whether a water body is inland or the sea
read a small table of lakes
SOCI.G5.RESOUR.FISHING_IN_KENYA.FISHING_.mastery: The child names Lake Victoria (the main inland fishing ground, in the west), Lake Turkana (north-west), Lake Naivasha, Lake Baringo and dams on the Tana River, knows the Indian Ocean is the sea and not inland, and knows Lake Magadi is a soda lake. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick a way fishing helps
say who earns from fishing
say why fishing should be controlled
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G5.RESOUR.FISHING_IN_KENYA.FISHING_.mastery: The child says fishing gives food and protein, jobs for fishers, traders and processors, money from selling fish at home and abroad (Nile perch fillets), and knows fish stocks must be protected from over-fishing. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: name the park from what it is known for
say where a park lies
pick the animal seen in a park
read a small table of parks
SOCI.G5.RESOUR.WILDLIFE_AND_TOURISM_IN_..mastery: The child links the Maasai Mara to the wildebeest migration (Narok), Amboseli to elephants and views of Mount Kilimanjaro (Kajiado), Tsavo to Kenya's largest park and red elephants (south-east), Lake Nakuru to flamingos and rhinos, Samburu to the Grevy's zebra (Isiolo), and the coast to beaches and marine parks. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick a benefit of tourism
say who earns from a park
say why wildlife must be protected
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G5.RESOUR.WILDLIFE_AND_TOURISM_IN_..mastery: The child says tourists bring foreign money, jobs (guides, drivers, hotel and craft workers) and income for local communities and park upkeep, so poaching and destroying wildlife homes harms the whole country. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the early means of transport
say what an early means carried
sort early and modern means
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G5.RESOUR.DEVELOPMENT_OF_TRANSPORT..mastery: The child names head and back loads carried by people, donkeys, camels and oxen, canoes and dhows, and trading caravans as early means, and sorts them from lorries, trains and aeroplanes. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the best means for a job
name the means from a description
say where a means runs
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G5.RESOUR.DEVELOPMENT_OF_TRANSPORT..mastery: The child picks road (matatus, buses, lorries), railway (the Standard Gauge Railway from Mombasa to Naivasha, built after the old railway from Mombasa to Kisumu), air (JKIA, Kisumu, Eldoret), water (ferries, lake steamers, the port of Mombasa) and pipeline (oil, fuel) for the right job. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the safe action
say why an action is unsafe
pick the safe place to cross
find the false step in a learner's plan
SOCI.G5.RESOUR.DEVELOPMENT_OF_TRANSPORT..mastery: The child picks safe actions: cross at a zebra crossing or footbridge after looking both ways, wear a seat belt or helmet on every trip, wait for a bus at the stop, keep off the road when playing, and says why unsafe actions put people in danger. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the early form of communication
say what a form was used for
sort early and modern forms
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G5.RESOUR.DEVELOPMENT_OF_COMMUNICA..mastery: The child names drums, horns, smoke signals, whistles, ululation and messengers or runners as early forms, says each carried news or warnings over a distance, and knows they were slower and reached fewer people than modern forms. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the best means for a job
say what a means can do that another cannot
say why a means helps a community
say a risk and how to stay safe
SOCI.G5.RESOUR.DEVELOPMENT_OF_COMMUNICA..mastery: The child names mobile phones, radio, television, newspapers, the post office and the internet, picks the right one for a job (radio for news to villages without electricity, post for parcels, phone for a quick call), and knows not everything online is true. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: name the leader from a description
say which community a leader led
say what a leader did
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G5.POLITI.TRADITIONAL_LEADERS_IN_K..mastery: The child links Mekatilili wa Menza to the Giriama and resistance to forced labour, Koitalel Arap Samoei to the Nandi and resistance to the railway, Nabongo Mumia to the Wanga kingdom and welcoming the British, Waiyaki wa Hinga to the Agikuyu of Dagoretti, and Lenana to the Maasai as a laibon. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the quality shown by an action
say why a leader was respected
say a role elders still play today
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G5.POLITI.TRADITIONAL_LEADERS_IN_K..mastery: The child names qualities shown (bravery, wisdom, honesty, fairness, unity) from what a leader did, and says elders still settle disputes, guide ceremonies and teach values in many communities. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say how a community was governed
pick the leader or council
say who made decisions
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G5.POLITI.EARLY_FORMS_OF_GOVERNM_E..mastery: The child says Kenyan communities had governments before colonial rule: councils of elders (Kikuyu Kiama, Meru Njuri Ncheke), age-sets, spiritual leaders (the Maasai laibon, the Meru Mugwe), clan heads, and kings among the Wanga, and does not say they had no rulers or that all had kings. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say what the two have in common
say how they differ

find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G5.POLITI.EARLY_FORMS_OF_GOVERNM_E..mastery: The child says both ruled through councils of elders and age-sets with no king; the Maasai had a laibon for spiritual guidance and warriors (morans) for defence; the Ameru had the Njuri Ncheke council of elders, who judged cases, and the Mugwe as spiritual leader. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the practice worth keeping
say how it is used today
say what to leave behind
find the false step in a learner's answer
SOCI.G5.POLITI.EARLY_FORMS_OF_GOVERNM_E..mastery: The child picks practices that still serve (consulting elders, settling quarrels by talk, leaders serving the community, young people given duties by age) and links each to today (mediation, public participation, community policing, youth service). Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say whether a person is a citizen
pick the ways to become a citizen
